claims.text: The gaps flow follows symlinked evidence files out of the project root: an evidence symlink to an outside file containing a passing result closes the gap with runner exit 0, because only the evidence directory chain is validated, never its contents.
boundary: engine gaps evidence discovery (companion issue only)

evidence.description: Phase 9 re-run P7b: evidence/linked.json symlink to an outside PASS file; runner exit 0, register Open: 0 | Closed: 1.
Reproduced on main 527feae with the real engine: symlinked evidence closed GAP-001 for T-API-001, runner exit 0, GAPS.md shows Open: 0 | Closed: 1.

falsification_tests: Run gaps with a symlinked evidence file pointing outside the project root and show the runner refusing (exit 2, offender named) with no gap closed — current behavior exits 0 and closes the gap.

claims.text: Generated assessment, challenge, and graph filenames use second-resolution timestamps, so two distinct runs in the same second share one filename: the ledger attests both contents while the file on disk holds only the second, silently losing the first assessment.

evidence.description: Phase 9 re-run S9: two different bundles in one second both named aee-after_plan-20261012T153725Z.json; ledger_entries=2, disk holds only the second.
Reproduced on main 527feae: markers A1/B1 both wrote aee-after_plan-20261012T160924Z.json; disk marker=B1 (second writer wins) while the ledger attests both.

falsification_tests: Run two distinct same-second assessments and show two distinct filenames whose contents each match their ledger record — current behavior collides on one name.

claims.text: The token-economy shell subcommand executes caller argv with no confinement: it runs in the caller's working directory rather than the project root, has no timeout, and writes the full argv — including secret values — verbatim into telemetry.

evidence.description: Phase 9 re-run P11/P11b/S11c: pwd printed the caller's directory; an outside-root file was printed verbatim; shell-calls.jsonl contains token=SUPERSECRETARG123 in full.
Reproduced on main 527feae: shell ran with caller cwd, printed an outside-root file, exit 0, and recorded the secret argv verbatim in telemetry.

falsification_tests: Run shell from outside the project and show it executing with cwd = project root, timing out on a hung command, and redacting secret-looking argv values in telemetry — current behavior does none of these.

claims.text: TOKEN_ROUTER_HOME lets an environment variable point at arbitrary out-of-root Python that route executes via sys.executable, and the router's range validation accepts JSON booleans as integers ([true, 3] becomes start=1); the route record names neither the router path nor its hash.

evidence.description: Phase 9 re-run P12: fake router outside the root executed; [[true, 3]] accepted as [1, 3]; route record has no router path/hash fields.
Reproduced on main 527feae: env-supplied out-of-root router ran, backend token-router, ranges [[1, 3]] from emitted [[true, 3]], exit 0.

falsification_tests: Point TOKEN_ROUTER_HOME outside the project and show the router never executes (deterministic fallback instead), bool ranges rejected, and an in-root router's path + SHA-256 recorded — current behavior executes it and coerces bools.

claims.text: No operation subprocess in run_aee.py has a timeout, so a hung engine hangs the spec-kit host workflow indefinitely with no diagnostic; only the version/help capability probes are time-bounded.
boundary: scripts/python/run_aee.py subprocess invocations for assess, challenge, graph, gaps, gate, review, verify

evidence.description: Phase 9 re-run E11: against an engine stub sleeping 60 s the runner did not return within 8 s; --help shows no --timeout option.
Reproduced on main 527feae: runner killed externally after 8 s against the sleeping stub; it never returned on its own.

falsification_tests: Run the runner against a hung engine with a short --timeout and show it returning exit 2 with a timed_out marker inside the bound — current behavior never returns.

claims.text: Every command template interpolates artifact/path placeholders unquoted into bash blocks, so a space-bearing or metacharacter path is word-split or substituted in the agent's shell even though the runner itself is injection-safe.

evidence.description: Templates at assess.md:32, challenge.md:18, gaps.md:28/34, gate.md:18, trace.md:18, verify.md:16, review.md:27, draft-claims.md:28 interpolate placeholders unquoted; probe P6 proved the runner itself safe.
Re-inspected on main 527feae: all run_aee.py / aee_token_economy.py invocation lines in commands/*.md still carry unquoted <...> placeholders and no verbatim-quoting guardrail line exists.

falsification_tests: Show every command template quoting its path placeholders and assess.md carrying the verbatim-quoting guardrail — current templates quote none.

claims.text: Lifecycle hooks fire commands with no bound phase or artifact, gate offers no --latest selection or freshness check, and no latest-assessment pointer exists, so gating a stale pre-fix assessment is one ambiguous path resolution away.

evidence.description: Phase 9 re-run E13: gate --help lists only --input; hooks are bare optional prompts with no phase/artifact binding; assess creates no latest-pointer file.
Confirmed on main 527feae: gate parser has only --input; extension.yml hooks carry no binding fields; no latest-<phase> pointer is written anywhere.

falsification_tests: Show gate --latest <phase> gating the assessment named by the assess-maintained pointer (refusing when none exists) and a documented per-hook artifact/phase table — current gate has neither.

claims.text: Install-facing docs drift from the shipped extension: the README installs the v1.0.1 archive while extension.yml declares 1.2.0, the README says this branch prepares 1.1.0 (unreleased), and the CHANGELOG heads both 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 as Unreleased although v1.2.0 is tagged.

evidence.description: Phase 9 doc inspection: README.md:63 installs v1.0.1.zip vs manifest 1.2.0; README.md:68 says 1.1.0 (unreleased); CHANGELOG heads both 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 Unreleased; no README-tag consistency test exists.
Re-confirmed on main 527feae and git tags: v1.2.0 tag exists (2026-10-06), no v1.1.0 tag exists; README and CHANGELOG text unchanged from the verdict.

falsification_tests: Show the README install tag equal to the manifest version with a test asserting it, and a CHANGELOG that dates shipped sections — current docs install 1.0.1 and call shipped work unreleased.

claims.text: check_install.py verifies only the local --dev install path and expresses every check as a bare assert, so the archive flow real users follow is never exercised and python -O silently strips all verification.

evidence.description: Phase 9 code inspection: only --evaluator-dir/--aee-dir local installs; no --from-archive mode; all checks are bare asserts (lines 28, 38, 47-49, 52, 54, 56, 68-69, 73, 75, 78, 85).
Re-read on main 527feae: same assert-based structure, local-directory installs only.

falsification_tests: Run check_install.py under python -O and against a release archive and show the checks still executing and able to fail loudly — current script verifies nothing under -O and has no archive mode.

claims.text: _safe_output returns the unresolved candidate path in both adapter scripts after validating its resolved form, leaving a check-then-use window in which a swapped path component redirects the engine's later write.

Re-read on main 527feae: both _safe_output implementations still return the unresolved candidate.

falsification_tests: Show _safe_output returning the resolved path in both scripts (a unit test asserts the returned path is absolute and resolved) — current code returns the unresolved candidate.

claims.text: route reads the entire target file into memory before any size or line gate, and two command docs misdescribe shipped behavior: route-evidence.md calls the deterministic fallback rg/grep (it is pure Python) and report-savings.md specifies used=<yes|no|n/a> while the helper emits JSON booleans.

evidence.description: Phase 9 inspection + live report run: _route does read_text().splitlines() on the whole file with no byte cap; route-evidence.md:49 describes rg/grep fallback; report-savings.md:47-48 specifies used=<yes|no|n/a> vs live JSON booleans.
Re-confirmed on main 527feae: _route still read_texts the whole file; both doc misdescriptions present verbatim.

falsification_tests: Show route refusing an over-cap file without loading it whole, and both docs matching the implementation — current code loads whole files and the docs misdescribe the fallback and the report shape.
